title: Samsung, SK hynix escalate Korea AI chip race with HBM4E and new memory - CHOSUNBIZ
key_facts: Samsung and SK hynix both unveiled seventh-generation HBM, HBM4E, at SEDEX 2026 in Seoul (opened 14 Oct 2026).
Samsung HBM4E: 14 to 16 Gbps per pin, more than 20% above HBM4, 3.6 TB/s, 12-high 48 GB stack; samples sent in May.
SK hynix HBM4E: up to 16 Gbps, more than 20% better energy efficiency; 12-high samples supplied in June.
Samsung showed zHBM, stacking HBM on top of the compute unit; SK hynix showed high-bandwidth flash (HBF) with about 10 times HBM capacity.
SK hynix's Ahn Hyeon said AI infrastructure performance will be about 20 times larger in 2030 than this year.
zHBM and HBF remain at concept and development stages.
quote_evidence: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix unveiled the seventh-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM), "HBM4E," side by side, kicking off a race in next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor technology.

However, since zHBM and HBF remain at the concept and development stages of next-generation technologies, the timing of commercialization and whether customers adopt them will likely determine their competitiveness.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory speed and placement are bottlenecks for AI chips, and the two largest HBM makers are racing on both.
